Estimated completion date passed two months ago and the record is 2.5 years stale.

Not read out. Registry record (API, read 2026-10-09): recruiting, last updated 2020-09-28, no results, estimated primary completion 2026-08, 3-year PFS, 508 planned. Europe PMC by registry number: 4 hits. Opened two: Transl Cancer Res 2026-03-25 (PMC13190708) calls it 'an ongoing phase III trial (NCT04448522)' testing 63.6 Gy in 30 fractions; BMJ 2026-02-10 (PMC12887725), from the same Sun Yat-sen group, mentions it as their separate phase 3 without any result. PubMed by reduced-dose + nasopharyngeal + induction chemotherapy: only the single-arm phase 2 of 60 Gy (5-year update, PMID 42150706), a different study. Beware sibling: NCT05304468 (60 vs 70 Gy, Sun Yat-sen), seen in search listings only. Two web searches (English by registry number; Chinese by design and dose) returned only registry mirrors. Design aims at equal tumour control with less toxicity, so it may be a non-inferiority design: flag for the exclusion review.

Registry record (API, read 2026-10-09): recruiting, last updated 2025-05-30, no results, estimated primary completion 2025-12, recurrence-free survival at 24 months, 213 planned. Opened the full text of the single-arm phase 1 research letter (BJS Open, doi 10.1093/bjsopen/zrag121, PMC13637039, PMID 42832193; PubMed date 2026-09-04, electronic publication 2026-10-05 in the XML): the 850 mg/m2 dose 'was therefore selected for the ongoing randomized phase III EFFIPEC trial' and 'Efficacy, recurrence outcomes, and comparative safety are being evaluated in the randomized phase III component'. That paper reports tolerability only and does not print the registry number; it cites the EFFIPEC protocol (PMID 38437211). Europe PMC and PubMed by acronym: protocol and phase 1 only. One web search (acronym, phase 3 results, investigator) found nothing further.
